title: Can you run batch jobs in Vert.x (setPeriodic, worker verticles/executeBlocking, Quartz cron)?
shortTitle: Can you run batch jobs in Vert.x (setPeriodic, worker verticles/executeBlocking, Quartz cron)?
keyPoints: Vert.x supports batch jobs with setPeriodic for fixed intervals and setTimer for one-shot delays, both firing on the event loop.
The timer handler must not block; its only job is to kick off heavy work on a worker verticle or executeBlocking.
Worker verticles and executeBlocking run on the worker pool and may block, keeping the event loop free for live requests.
For calendar-style cron scheduling, integrate the Vert.x Quartz extension or compute the next fire time and arm a timer.
In a clustered deployment, use leader election or a distributed lock to prevent every node from running the same batch job.
Long batch jobs should be idempotent, chunked, and restartable so a crash mid-batch can be recovered safely.

s1_definition.oneliner: Schedule the trigger on the event loop with setPeriodic or a cron timer, but always run the heavy batch work on a worker verticle or executeBlocking.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **setPeriodic** – fires a handler on the event loop at a fixed interval and returns a timer id you can cancel.
- **setTimer** – fires a handler once after a delay, useful for one-shot scheduling.
- **executeBlocking** – runs a blocking lambda on the worker thread pool and returns a `Future`, keeping the event loop free.
- **Worker verticle** – a verticle deployed with `setWorker(true)` that runs entirely on worker threads and may block.
- **Cron scheduling** – for calendar-based triggers (every weekday at 2 AM), integrate Quartz or compute the next fire time and arm a timer.
s1_definition.analogy: Imagine National Bank of India must run an end-of-day interest posting job. The fast front-desk clerk (event loop) is not the one who should sit crunching thousands of accounts because that would freeze the counter. Instead, the clerk keeps a timer on his desk (setPeriodic) that rings every interval, and when it rings he hands the heavy ledger work to the back-office team (worker verticle) so the counter keeps serving customers. For jobs that must run at a specific wall-clock time like 2 AM on business days, the bank uses a calendar scheduler (Quartz cron) that wakes the back office at exactly the right moment.

```text
  Batch Job Flow in Vert.x:

  ┌───────────────┐   tick    ┌───────────────┐
  │ setPeriodic / │──────────▶│  Event Loop    │
  │ setTimer /    │           │  (handler)     │
  │ Quartz cron   │           │                │
  └───────────────┘           │  DO NOT block  │
                              │  here!         │
                              └───────┬────────┘
                                      │ delegate
                                      ▼
                              ┌───────────────┐
                              │ executeBlocking│
                              │ or Worker      │
                              │ Verticle       │
                              │                │
                              │ Heavy batch    │
                              │ work runs here │
                              └───────┬────────┘
                                      │ complete
                                      ▼
                              ┌───────────────┐
                              │ Callback on    │
                              │ Event Loop     │
                              │ (onSuccess)    │
                              └───────────────┘

  Cluster-Safe Execution:
  ┌──────┐  ┌──────┐  ┌──────┐
  │Node 1│  │Node 2│  │Node 3│
  └──┬───┘  └──┬───┘  └──┬───┘
     │ try     │ try     │ try
     │ lock    │ lock    │ lock
     ▼         ▼         ▼
  ┌──────────────────────────┐
  │  Distributed Lock        │
  │  (only one wins)         │
  └──────────────────────────┘
     │
     ▼
  Node 1 runs the batch
  Nodes 2, 3 skip
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Yes, Vert.x runs batch and scheduled jobs well, as long as you respect the golden rule of never blocking the event loop. For simple fixed-rate scheduling, use setPeriodic, which fires a handler on the event loop at an interval and returns a timer id you can cancel. The crucial discipline is that the timer handler itself does almost nothing; its only job is to kick off the real work somewhere safe. The heavy batch processing goes onto worker threads, either through executeBlocking or inside a dedicated worker verticle, and for isolation create a sized shared worker executor so batch work never starves ordinary tasks.

For calendar-style cron scheduling, setPeriodic alone is not enough because it only does fixed intervals. Use the Vert.x Quartz extension or a cron parser to compute the delay until the next fire time, arm a timer for that delay, run the job on a worker, and re-arm for the following occurrence.

At National Bank of India Rajesh built exactly this for daily interest posting. A batch verticle schedules the trigger, and when it fires it submits the interest job to a dedicated worker pool via executeBlocking, so the event loop stays free to serve live balance and transfer requests. The job walks each account, computes the daily interest on the balance using BigDecimal, credits Rajesh and Priya, and returns the total. It is written to be idempotent and chunked so it can be retried safely after a crash. In production the job runs on a cron schedule, and because the deployment is a Vert.x cluster, a distributed lock ensures only the leader node executes the run so the bank never double-posts interest.

Remember one sentence: schedule the trigger on the event loop with setPeriodic or a cron timer, but always push the actual batch work onto a worker verticle or executeBlocking so the event loop stays free.
